newsitem.title: USA: Florida West airline expands Miami facilities.
newsitem.headline: Florida West airline expands Miami facilities.

text.p: Florida West International Airlines, an all-cargo airline, has moved into new facilities at Miami International Airport, expanding its warehouse capacity dramatically, its chief executive said.
"We have moved into a new cargo building and already are handling cargo there. Our offices will move in May," Florida West president Richard Haberly told Reuters.
The new space is 75,000 square feet with 12 cargo doors, compared with about 12,000 sq ft and only two doors before the move, he said.

Florida West is flying three times a week to Brazil with a Boeing 747 leased from Atlas Air Cargo. It is using its Douglas DC-8 for one trip per week to Brazil, one to Buenos Aires and one to Peru, Haberly said.
Florida West has been ordered by the U.S. Department of Transportation to find a replacement for its majority owner, an Iranian-born American citizen named Mansour Rasnavid by August this year.
On the issue of new investors, Haberly would say only "we are still considering our options regarding investors." -Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
